Sports.title: Kalpana shows guts to go with her class in Yorkshire Oaks
Sports.content:
King George heroine Kalpana just held on to land the Legends Global Yorkshire Oaks at York after a mighty scare from Sparan Nua.

Aidan O'Brien's outsider Sugar Island was immediately sent to the front and Ronan Whelan quickly distanced himself from the field, extending the advantage to 20 lengths turning for home.

But as the main players began to eat into that lead, Colin Keane sent Kalpana to give chase over three furlongs out, hitting top gear two furlongs from home, only for Jim Bolger's Sparan Nua - who got a little squeezed at one stage - to make up plenty of ground and close the gap.

The line just came in time for the 10-11 favourite to hold on by a short head, giving Keane, Andrew Balding and owners Juddmonte a second Group One in the space of 24 hours, after Item had landed the showpiece Juddmonte International on Wednesday.

"You knew after going a couple of furlongs it was going to be messy and passing the three (furlong marker) I thought the pacemaker was gone," said Juddmonte's European racing manager Barry Mahon.

"Colin had to commit probably a bit sooner than he wanted. When he saw himself the pacemaker was gone he had to chase her down a little bit, so she was always going to be vulnerable to something closing late, but she's gutsy and knows where the line is.

"She put her head down and got the job done. It's not pretty, but she got the job done and that's the main thing.

"Fast ground, slow ground, 12 furlongs - you wouldn't even be afraid to drop her back to 10. She's just very versatile and the ultimate pro now. She's fully matured now at five years of age and keeps answering all the questions, so it's wonderful."

Connections must now consider how to split their aces, with either Kalpana or Item likely to get a shot at the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe.

Should Item be given the green light to head for ParisLongchamp, Kalpana - who finished seventh in last year's Arc - will almost certainly bid to win the Qipco British Champions Fillies & Mares Stakes at Ascot later in October.

Mahon added: "We have the horse from yesterday too, so whether he'll go to the Arc and we wait for Ascot with this filly - we have to sit down in a week or two and discuss all that, but it's a nice problem to have.

"The horse from yesterday has joined the fray, so we'll decide all those sort of things in the next couple of weeks with the owners and see what they want to do.

"Item is definitely a top of the ground horse. He got away with the good to soft here yesterday. Funnily enough Colin actually said this filly doesn't enjoy the softer ground as much as she did last year, he said she felt like she enjoyed the faster ground in Ascot more the last time than she did today.

"I wouldn't have thought we'd run both in the Arc. Again that will be the owners' decision, but it wouldn't be my first preference.

"I suppose with Item being a colt, if the ground comes up good he'd probably have the preference, and with this filly Ascot was always the target, so it would make sense to sidestep the Arc if the ground is good - but that's a big 'if'.

"She probably will retire at the end of the year. Whether she'll finish at Ascot or if she doesn't go to the Arc whether she'll go to the Breeders' Cup - there's a lot of variables to work out."

Sports.title: Hamilton urges Ferrari to 'apply pressure' to Antonelli in title battle
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has urged his Ferrari team to "apply the pressure" to title rival Kimi Antonelli as he seeks to chase down the Mercedes driver in the championship battle.

The 2026 Formula 1 season resumes at the Dutch Grand Prix this weekend following the sport's summer break, with Antonelli leading Hamilton by 50 points at the top of the standings.

There is a huge gap in experience between the pair, with the 41-year-old Hamilton chasing a record eighth drivers' title, while Antonelli, who turns 20 two days after Sunday's race in Zandvoort, is seeking a maiden championship in just his second F1 campaign.

Hamilton said: "There are pros and cons to it. He's obviously very fast. He's doing an amazing job.

"When you are 19 you don't really have much else going on in your life really, so you don't have many other pressures. I remember when I was that age and things are relatively easier in life, I would say.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the F1 Show podcast, David Croft questions whether Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton can challenge Kimi Antonelli for this season's world championship.

"Nonetheless, it's not saying he hasn't still got a hard job ahead of him, but he's been doing great.

"I'm not really looking at any weaknesses because I don't think he has shown any this season. I think we've got to just work hard to just continue to apply the pressure."

Mercedes generally had a faster car than Ferrari over the opening 11 rounds of the season, but Hamilton is hoping more upgrades from the Italian team, some of which will be available in Zandvoort, can aid his cause.

"Hopefully we are going to continue to progress in development," Hamilton said.

"The team are working really hard. We've got our first little step this weekend which I'm really grateful for because they are under a huge amount of pressure to continue to bring parts, as every team is.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Relive what some of the Formula One drivers, including Lewis Hamilton, George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, got up to during the summer break!

"But we are going in the right direction with the car. Obviously, Mercedes are still the leaders. McLaren are now up in there and obviously Red Bull are now super quick so there are four teams that are all very close.

"But we just focus on doing our job the best we can. I think we can do a better job in the second half, so that's our goal."

Hamilton 'massively driven' to claim first Dutch GP win

Zandvoort is one of just four circuits on F1's 2026 calendar that Hamilton hasn't previously won at.

The Brit is yet to top the podium in Miami and Las Vegas, which were added to the schedule in 2022 and 2023, respectively, while Madrid is hosting F1 for the first time in September.

Hamilton qualified and finished second when the Dutch Grand Prix returned to F1's schedule in 2021, but has failed to make the podium again since.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hamilton CRASHES OUT of wet Dutch Grand Prix!

With Zandvoort dropping off the calendar next year, and there seeming to be little prospect of it returning any time soon, Hamilton says he is highly motivated to claim victory.

He said: "I've won at pretty much all the other tracks, but I don't think I've won here before, so I definitely want to change that. I'm massively driven.

"It's just such an incredible circuit, great crowd here, very special particularly for Max as he comes here and has the incredible support through the weekend. They really create the atmosphere.

"It's a track I've yet to really truly conquer in Formula 1, so it's definitely something I want to try to do this weekend."

Antonelli: One of my opponents is also myself

Antonelli exceeded all expectations to build a significant lead over the first half of the season, which could have been significantly bigger if it weren't for some major misfortune.

The Italian retired from second place with an engine failure when Hamilton won in Barcelona, and appeared to be on course for victory at Silverstone when a wheel-guard failure dropped him out of the points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli suffers damage during the British Grand Prix.

Antonelli's speed has been so consistent that the chasing pack's biggest hope for the remaining 12 rounds would appear to be errors creeping into his driving.

Antonelli said: "It's going to be a very intense second half of the season but I'm ready. I'm looking forward to the challenge and hopefully it's going to be a great one."

"I know the expectations are very high but, on my side, I just need to keep delivering the results, keep doing my job the best way I can without worrying about [the] championship or anything like that.

"I don't want to go in the car driving thinking about [the] championship or being afraid to do mistakes or stuff like that. Of course, there will be times where I might think more before doing something but, other than that, I just want to enjoy it as much as possible and be free all the way. Then we'll see where we end up at the end of the year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ride onboard as Kimi Antonelli crashes into Charles Leclerc during the 2025 Dutch Grand Prix.

"We could say one of my opponents is also myself. That's why it's really important to keep having a solid mind, a solid mindset. Always have the focus on the right things and always go in the car with the right mindset, a good level of intensity and then keep working with the people that I trust in case I need them. Also try to make the best use of it.

"Of course, it's going to be a very intense second half with a lot of triple headers, a lot of travelling, going in a lot different places, but I'm really excited and really looking forward to it. I am ready to embrace the challenge and hopefully it's going to be a great second half."

Sports.title: Premier League returns and Arsenal sense opportunity with rivals in flux
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta wants to get his messaging absolutely right. According to him, Arsenal are not about to defend their Premier League title. They are set to attack another one.

Remember Win the dog, who the manager brought in to the club’s training ground a few years back? She must now be called “Won”. But it is when Arteta quibbles over another bout of semantics that he highlights why he is entering the new season with such energy and optimism.

Do not talk to him about Arsenal’s stability. He prefers the word “consistency” along with more thrusting ones like “ambition”. The overall theme is clear. When Arteta surveys the landscape at the top end of the English game, he sees a settled environment at his club and flux elsewhere.

In terms of the so-called Big Six – the richest clubs in the country, as ranked by Deloitte – there are new managers at Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea; a virtually new one at Tottenham and a relatively new one at Manchester United. It has been a summer of unprecedented change in the Premier League with nine clubs with a new man in charge. Of those who hold out hope of a title challenge, only Aston Villa have a fully bedded-in manager in Unai Emery.

Rather abruptly, Arteta finds himself as the longest-serving manager in the division; he took over from Emery at Arsenal in December 2019. Emery is second on the list, having been at Villa for three years and nine months, and only one other – Daniel Farke at Leeds – has been at his club for more than three years.

When Arteta was given the job at Arsenal, Pep Guardiola was two titles into his storied City tenure, Jürgen Klopp had won the Champions League at Liverpool and was on his way to winning the league that season and José Mourinho had just joined Spurs.

View image in fullscreen Mikel Arteta and Arsenal held their nerve to hold off the challenge from Manchester City last season. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Arteta has seen them all off, with Guardiola’s departure from City at the end of last season being the most significant single shift in the dynamics for the forthcoming campaign.

Arteta is now the big beast, the only current manager to have won the Premier League, and as Arsenal prepare for the curtain-raiser at home to Coventry on Friday night, it is hard to ignore the confidence they are projecting. With virtually of all their rivals in transition, uncertainty undercutting the excitement, predictions difficult to make in the face of little actual evidence, Arsenal are reassured by their firm foundations. They sense opportunity, another title; the creation of a dynasty. That is the ultimate goal.

There is something more. Namely how everything changed for them in the closing weeks of last season. City had done the hard work, clawing back a nine-point deficit from the middle of March – a period when they had a game in hand. But in the five-match shootout that followed, City blinked first, drawing at Everton. Most know how nerve-racking it was for Arsenal. Not least Arteta. The Emirates Stadium was a sea of anxiety when Arsenal last played there – against Burnley in the penultimate game of the season. They got a 1-0 win over the line.

View image in fullscreen Bruno Guimarães is a high-quality arrival from Newcastle to boost Arsenal’s midfield ranks. Photograph: Mark Leech/Offside/Getty Images

Then City drew at Bournemouth and it was over; Arsenal’s 22-year wait, the oppressive weight. It is impossible to underestimate the feeling of liberation. Nobody can question the bottle of this team. Nobody will taunt them with the cry of “second again, olé, olé.” It is plain Arteta and his players will feed off it and perhaps it will lead to a more expansive style of football. The fear of falling short inhibited their game as the heat rose last time out.

Arsenal have made changes behind the scenes, looking for the marginal gains, most notably in the medical department where the head doctor, Zafar Iqbal, was mutually consented in early June. Arnaldo Abrantes has come in from Aston Villa to replace him. If the players can stay fitter for longer, Arsenal believe they can stay ahead. They have protected themselves with moves to deepen an already well-stocked squad. Bruno Guimarães is the most eye-catching addition, with Ezri Konsa about to follow.

Arsenal versus City still feels like the primary head-to-head. Guardiola had Arteta’s number last season, winning two and drawing one of the three meetings between the clubs. City were much the better team in the Carabao Cup final that they won 2-0. But that was under Guardiola and that was with Rodri and Bernardo Silva. If Guardiola’s exit has hit City the hardest, then those of the commanding midfielders to Barcelona and Real Madrid, respectively, is not far behind.

City’s faith in their new manager, Enzo Maresca, is rooted in what they saw of him when he worked on their coaching staff; he was an assistant to Guardiola in the treble-winning season of 2022-23. Previously, he coached the Under‑23s to the Premier League 2 title in 2020-21.

View image in fullscreen Elliot Anderson has arrived at Manchester City for £116m, but, like his manager, he has big shoes to fill. Photograph: Alex Pantling/FA/Getty Images

It is a well-thought-through appointment; the kind a well-run club makes. Yet at the same time, it is not one to quicken the pulse. Maresca, quite simply, has enormous shoes to fill. Ditto Elliot Anderson, the impressive young midfielder upon whom City have bet the house. Can City be better given the personnel losses they have sustained? They must surely do so given the direction of travel at Arsenal. City do retain the cheat code that is Erling Haaland.

There are parallels between City and Liverpool, who want their new manager, Andoni Iraola, to have a similar impact in his first season that Arne Slot managed in 2024-25. Slot took Klopp’s team and glided to the title. Maybe consistency in the dugout is not everything?

On the other hand, Slot was given only one new player – Federico Chiesa – who barely played that season and he essentially stuck with what had made the Klopp collective so successful. It was evolution not revolution. When he tried the latter last season, Slot found that his tenure unravelled, although his rotten luck with injuries must be acknowledged. There was also the death of Diogo Jota.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Liverpool have moved on Andy Robertson, Ibrahima Konaté and, most crucially, Mohamed Salah, even if he was a shadow of his former self last season. Salah has not yet been replaced; it would be impossible to replace the prime-years version of him and Iraola, who has a number of injury concerns, has it all to do.

Coaxing more from Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak is fundamental. Iraola’s style has the capacity to hold Anfield in thrall; the aggression, the front-foot slickness, the boldness to go one-versus-one all over the pitch. How quickly can he impose it?

Chelsea will be interesting under Xabi Alonso, who has been allowed to add players to fit into the 3-4-2-1 he used to such stunning effect at Bayer Leverkusen. Alonso has also been permitted to break from the club’s youth-first signing model and bring in much-needed experience.

View image in fullscreen Morgan Rogers celebrates scoring in pre-season, after his £117m move from Aston Villa. Photograph: Anthony Hanc/Wired Photos/Shutterstock

Morgan Rogers, alongside Cole Palmer and behind João Pedro, with Moisés Caicedo and maybe Reece James in the deep midfield roles, has a very nice feel to it. There is talent in central defence. The lack of European football will be a temporary blessing.

Ask any chief executive what supporters want at the start of a season and the answer is invariably the same: be better than last season. Which will not be a problem for Chelsea after the implosion to limp home in 10th. Or Spurs, who finished 17th for the second campaign in a row and narrowly avoided relegation. Roberto De Zerbi, who was appointed as the manager with seven games to go, kept them up and in the first summer since the end of Daniel Levy’s near 25-year as chair, the new hierarchy have been determined to act decisively. Their heavy spend on Premier League-proven players has allowed the fanbase to dream.

De Zerbi is a man to generate buy-in. In him they trust. Ditto a midfield that will feature Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes. With Conor Gallagher or James Maddison expected to fill the No 10 role, Spurs look to have a proper unit to hold things together. They will also benefit from no European football.

What about United, for whom everything suddenly came together after the appointment of Michael Carrick in January, initially for an interim spell? His record meant the club had to give him the job on a permanent basis – he finished the season with 12 wins and three draws from 17 league matches. It was 2.3 points per game. Transpose that over a 38-match campaign and you get 87 points. Arsenal won the title with 85. Are United dark horses for glory?

Concerns remain. Carrick was largely untroubled by injuries and when United have their best XI on the field they are a match for anybody. When they miss a few, as they normally did under Ruben Amorim, they can flatline. United were always going to have to add a good number of signings this summer, particularly as they prepare to go from a Europe-free season to a return to the Champions League. They have not yet done enough; the final week-and-a-half of the transfer window could be crucial. As Mike Tyson almost said, everybody has a plan until they are punched in the face by the Champions League.

View image in fullscreen Marcus Rashford is back at Manchester United after falling out of favour during Ruben Amorim’s reign. Photograph: Grzegorz Wajda/SOPA/Getty Images

Are Villa really about to take another step forward after the highs of last season when they finished fourth and won the Europa League? It feels unlikely given the departures, headlined by those of Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, with Konsa primed to go, too. Strangely, there is a whiff of transition about them. It is possible to find reasons to fret about every team. Apart from Arsenal.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 19: Sunderland
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 14th (NB: this is not necessarily Louise Taylor’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 7th

Prospects

After finishing seventh last season, Sunderland go into the new campaign engaged in continental combat for the first time since a brief adventure in the old Cup Winners’ Cup in 1973-74. Will their startling upward trajectory under Régis Le Bris continue or will they succumb to the dreaded second-season syndrome? No one is quite sure.

While many like to highlight Sunderland’s relegation-level XG statistics last season, it is important to note that a steadily improving squad lost six players to the Africa Cup of Nations in the winter. Moreover, no key player has been sold this summer, team spirit is superb and pre-season performances have been reassuringly convincing. Le Bris accepts coping with Thursday night football will be a challenge for a club that played in League One as recently as 2022, but insists it is something to be enjoyed rather than feared.

It helps that Sunderland still have their captain, Granit Xhaka, controlling midfield. If Xhaka’s decision to recommit to life at the Stadium of Light despite serious interest from Chelsea lifted the pre-season mood, further optimism is provided by the presence of high-calibre individuals, including the fans’ favourite Enzo Le Fée, Chris Rigg, Robin Roefs, Noah Sadiki and Nordi Mukiele, in a versatile squad containing several players comfortable in assorted positions. Brian Brobbey is the sort of robust centre-forward few defenders enjoy marking. “We are growing together,” says Le Bris. “We’ve shown the team is strong.”

Off-field picture

Sunderland are majority-owned by the 29-year-old Swiss-French businessman and trust fund billionaire Kyril Louis-Dreyfus. The son of the late former Marseille owner Robert Louis-Dreyfus has a 64%stake in the club while the remaining 36% is held by the Uruguayan businessman and politician Juan Sartori. The strong relationship between Le Bris and the director of football, Florent Ghisolfi, has helped ensure on-pitch stability, although the past year has brought considerable off-field change, with several key executives replaced as Sunderland’s commercial strategy pivots in a more international direction. While the team toured the United States this summer, other marketing efforts have been concentrated on Africa, with a lucrative, and controversial, front-of-shirt sponsorship with Visit Ghana close to being finalised. More locally, the regeneration of the area adjacent to the Stadium of Light is transforming a post-industrial landscape.

Owner-fan relationship

If Louis-Dreyfus initially attracted a degree of suspicion and scepticism on taking the helm in 2021, he has earned the trust of the fanbase. Supporters were particularly impressed that the owner contacted Xhaka and convinced the Switzerland captain to join from Bayer Leverkusen last summer. Less positively, a creep towards increased corporate hospitality, allied to a divisive new club membership scheme, has polarised season-ticket holders.

The manager

Le Bris enjoys a spot of close-season surfing on the beaches of his native Brittany, so it is perhaps appropriate that the 50-year-old rode a footballing wave last season. His 2025 Championship playoff winners hit the Premier League ground running and proved they could last the course. Along the way, Le Bris parked his tanks on Newcastle’s front lawn by choreographing two league wins over their rivals. Le Bris holds a doctorate in physiology and biomechanics and a diploma in the mental training of elite athletes. He spent a decade as a highly regarded youth coach at Lorient before taking charge of the first team in 2022, with his love of trigonometry underpinning a coaching philosophy that views football as fundamentally being about triangles.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Thomas Meunier, who has 83 caps for Belgium, has joined Sunderland on a two-year contract from Lille. Photograph: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images

Sunderland tried and failed to sign Thomas Meunier from Lille a year ago, but patience has been rewarded. At the time of writing, the 34-year-old free transfer is the sole summer signing – quite a contrast to the 14 new faces 12 months ago – but at least two more new recruits are expected before the window closes. Meunier, who has 83 Belgium caps and played at the World Cup, will compete with Mukiele and Trai Hume at right-back. The experience he has acquired throughout a career involving stints at Paris Saint-Germain and Borussia Dortmund should prove useful in the Europa League.

Stat attack

If matches were decided by Opta’s expected points metric, Sunderland would have been relegated last season. Instead they are preparing for a Europa League campaign after finishing 11 places higher than the XG figures implied they deserved. It was a wider margin between statistical performance and outcome than any other team in Europe’s big five leagues experienced, for good or bad.

Set for a breakthrough

Tom Proctor, the son of Sunderland’s first-team coach and former forward, Michael Proctor, is only 17 and starting his second year as an academy scholar.He was included in the first-team squad for the pre-season tour of the United States. Proctor has impressed with his technical ability, awareness and eye for goal. With the squad set to be stretched by Europa League involvement, it will be no surprise if a player who joined Sunderland’s academy at the age of six makes a competitive first-team debut this season.

World Cup impact

Sunderland had 12 players at the World Cup, more than Real Madrid, and such visibility delighted executives charged with growing the club’s commercial revenue streams. Wilson Isidor scored Haiti’s first World Cup goal since 1974 while Brobbey struck three times for the Netherlands. The entire group has since been joined by Meunier, who represented Belgium in the United States.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino eyes junior tournament in Dominican Republic as potential route out of crisis
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino wants to split the European and North American coalition that is seeking to oust him by attending a junior tournament in the Dominican Republic this weekend in another gamble to cling on to power from the Fifa president.

The Guardian has learned that Infantino has made plans to attend the U14 Boys Challenge competition organised by the Caribbean Football Union (CFU), 21 of whose associations are voting members of Fifa, despite being urged to stay away from the event by senior figures within Concacaf – the Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football – which is working with Uefa to remove him.

Infantino will come face-to-face with the man widely viewed as his most credible challenger, the Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, if he follows through with his intention to travel to the Dominican Republic, whose FA invited him to attend before the World Cup sell-off plan emerged last month.

The Dominican Republic has since backed the joint Uefa, Concacaf and Asian Football Confederation statement calling for Infantino to hold an independent review of the Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, as well as an emergency meeting of the Fifa council.

Infantino has largely fallen back on the support of his most steadfast allies by spending time in Morocco and Qatar as the storm has raged over the last month, but is understood to view the CFU meetings as a good opportunity split the Concacaf block and lobby for votes from the region’s smaller nations before next March’s presidential election.

Concacaf’s most successful nation, Mexico, is defying the confederation by backing Infantino, who has also received support from two CFU members, Grenada and St Kitts and Nevis.

View image in fullscreen Victor Montagliani, the Concacaf president, will be at the tournament in the Dominican Republic. Photograph: Omar Vega/Getty Images

The Boys Challenge and CFU meetings are not Fifa events, so Infantino’s plan to attend has raised eyebrows. Fifa declined to comment when asked about the president’s movements.

Uefa, Concacaf and the AFC are continuing to explore calling for a vote of no confidence in Infantino, which would bring the matter to a head before next year’s election.

Under Fifa’s statutes, its council can convene an extraordinary congress at any time if 43 of Fifa’s 211 member associations submit a written request specifying the items they want on the agenda, which can include no-confidence votes.

An extraordinary congress must then be convened within three months, although the governing body’s statutes contain no specific provision regarding a vote of no confidence in its president.

Infantino came under renewed pressure on Thursday with worldwide fans’ groups launching a petition calling for his resignation.

Fans are being encouraged to sign the petition, which already has support from all six Fifa confederations spanning continental and national fan groups.

“The shameful attempt by one individual – the Fifa president himself – to sell off the World Cup to private investors exposed a betrayal football will never forget,” a statement on behalf of the fan organisations said. “Infantino’s plan was stitched together in secret. Negotiated behind closed doors. Hidden from Fifa’s own members and from the millions of people whose passion makes football what it is.

“A president who repeatedly betrays football and makes a mockery of our game has lost the right to lead it,” the statement continued. “For the credibility of Fifa – and for the future of the game – he must resign.”

Sports.title: European playoffs: Rangers scrape first-leg win as Brighton draw in Norway
Sports.content:
Ryan Naderi’s second-half strike gave an unconvincing Rangers a narrow 1-0 win in the first leg of their Conference League playoff tie against Czech side Jablonec at Ibrox. Derek McInnes got his first win as Rangers manager at the fifth time of asking with a 5-1 thumping of St Mirren on Sunday but there was regression in the goalless first half which brought boos at the interval whistle.

The Govan side pepped up after the break and Naderi opened the scoring from close range in the 50th minute but in the 78th minute the substitute Cammy Devlin was sent off – minutes after coming off the bench – for a high tackle on Jiri Slama to leave Rangers to see out the game with 10 men.

Fabian Hürzeler, admitted: “It’s not the result we hoped for,” after Brighton were held to a frustrating goalless draw against Tromsø in Norway. The Seagulls, who open the new domestic campaign against Aston Villa on Sunday, created several good chances but could not find a way past the Tromsø keeper Jakob Haugaard.

View image in fullscreen Brighton players applaud the fans after their draw at Tromsø. Photograph: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images

The winger Ibrahim Osman – making his Brighton debut after three loan spells away – looked particularly lively during the first half. Tromsø then almost snatched a late winner on the break, but the defender Isak Vadebu sent his shot wide as the tie went into next week’s second leg at the Amex Stadium all square.

Hearts’ head coach, Wouter Vrancken, hopes James Wilson’s stunning goal in the 2-2 Conference League draw with Rapid Vienna is a sign of things to come from the youngster. He drilled in an unstoppable drive from 30 yards just moments after coming on as the hosts took the lead in the playoff first leg.

“He’s a young lad so for sure it will be extra special. Let’s hope he can make the next steps,” Vrancken said.

Wilson’s effort marked an impressive turnaround after Josh McPade cancelled out Serge-Philippe Raux-Yao’s first-half header. However, Rapid scrambled in a late equaliser through Nikolaus Wumbrand to ensure the tie remains on a knife edge ahead of next week’s return leg.

David Gray, the Hibernian head coach, savoured “a massive performance and a massive result” as his side kept themselves on course to reach the main phase with a spirited 0-0 draw in Belgium against Gent.

For the second Thursday night in a row, Hibs ground out a stalemate on foreign soil after they eliminated Shkendija in North Macedonia last week. It could have been even better for them if Owen Elding’s 15th-minute penalty had not been saved by Davy Roef.

Motherwell made a whirlwind start at home to Freiburg, with Regan Charles-Cook sidefooting in Emmanuel Longelo’s cutback after just 73 seconds. But Matthias Ginter headed Freiburg level on 27 minutes and netted a second from the spot, after Martin Moormann was shown a straight red card on 65 minutes via a video assistant referee review.

The substitute Keisuke Goto added a third with a stoppage-time header to leave the Scottish side with a 3-1 deficit mountain to climb in Germany next Thursday.

The Northern Irish champions, Larne, took a big step towards the league phase after a 2-0 win at 10-man Lincoln Red Imps.

The match looked set to finish goalless in Gibraltar after Red Imps had held firm following Yussef Flalhi’s 29th-minute red card. However, visiting Larne made their pressure pay when Paul O’Neill struck with five minutes left before fellow substitute Kevin O’Hara’s stoppage-time breakaway goal ensured Gary Haveron’s side will have a cushion ahead of the second leg at Inver Park.

Shamrock were held to a 1-1 draw at home by the Finnish side KuPS after they conceded an 85th-minute equaliser. The former Sheffield United full-back Enda Stevens put the Irish side ahead after 49 minutes, but they were denied a precious victory when the one-time Charlton youngster Piotr Parzyszek levelled late on at Tallaght Stadium.

View image in fullscreen Mohamed Salah had a tricky night against Ferencvaros. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

In the Europa League, Mohamed Salah played all 90 minutes of his home debut as Trabzonspor hosted Ferencvaros, but the Hungarian side won 1-0 and their Turkish opponents had Chibuike Nwaiwu sent off in added time.

Sports.title: ‘Enzo is a Chelsea player,’ says Alonso but doesn’t guarantee Fernández’s future
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso has refused to offer any guarantee that Chelsea will hold firm if Manchester City try to sign Enzo Fernández.

Fernández’s future remains up in the air and the prospect of him leaving Stamford Bridge has not gone away, even though Chelsea’s unofficial deadline for clubs to make written bids of £120m for the 25-year-old Argentina midfielder has already passed. City, who are also tracking Roma’s Manu Koné, have targeted Fernández as part of their midfield rebuild after Rodri’s move to Barcelona and are weighing up whether to make a move before the transfer window shuts.

Chelsea, who have identified Bournemouth’s Alex Scott and Crystal Palace’s Adam Wharton as possible replacements for Fernández, know the situation is fluid. The player has made no secret of his desire to leave the club and Alonso was noncommittal when asked if he would still be part of his squad at the end of the transfer window.

“Enzo is a Chelsea player,” the former Real Madrid manager said. “He’s a top player. He’s training really well since he started 10 days ago with the team. Very integrated, and we are happy with him. He’s getting ready for Monday.”

Chelsea open their Premier League campaign with a trip to Fulham on Monday night. Fernández is expected to be in the squad but Alonso dodged another question about whether the £106.7m midfielder has told him he wants to stay. “He’s training really well. I see him with a good attitude. That’s what we want. Everyone is trying their best to prepare for the kick off of the Premier League.”

Chelsea will want a new midfielder if Fernández goes. They are huge admirers of Scott but have already failed with one offer for the 22-year-old and have been told that Bournemouth will resist a sale this summer. Wharton is an alternative, although City have had an offer for the England midfielder rejected by Palace.

Alonso is also looking to trim down his squad before the window shuts. Nicolas Jackson, Liam Delap and Marc Guiu have fallen down the pecking order up front and are likely to leave. Everton, Leeds, Ipswich and Nottingham Forest are tracking Delap. Chelsea also have interest in Pedro Neto and Malo Gusto while Palace want to bolster their defence by signing Axel Disasi on loan.

It has been another busy summer at Chelsea and Alonso must also consider whether keeping Fernández would sit well with supporters. Some booed him during the friendly win over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge last week. “He was not just booed, they as well chanted his name,” Alonso said. “It’s not unusual, it can happen. We support him. We have a great player with Enzo, he’s a top player, he’s been so important.”

There was a reminder of Fernández’s standing when he wore the captain’s armband after coming on against Sociedad. Alonso could continue to use him as Reece James’s deputy. “Reece is the first captain and we have other leaders, other personalities that share the same role,” the Spaniard added.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick rejects ‘ridiculous’ talk of easy start to Manchester United season
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick has dismissed suggestions that Manchester United’s opening two games against Hull and Ipswich represent a favourable start to the season. United travel to Hull for Saturday’s opening match before hosting Ipswich a week on Sunday. Both sides were promoted from the Championship.

Carrick is adamant neither game will prove easy. “For all of us to know this league, there’s no favourable start, I think it’s a tough start,” he said. “A promoted team away from home is a tough game.

“I’ve been involved in them in the past so I’m fully aware of what’s coming at us on Saturday, what we’ve got to be ready for. So it’s not favourable. It’s an easy thing to throw out there. But it’s pretty ridiculous in a certain way, [we are] not taking it that way at all.”

Carrick guided United to third last season after taking interim charge in January. He became permanent manager four months later on the back of his success in the role. He was asked if leading United to the title this season is a realistic ambition. “It is going to be a jump,” said the 45-year-old. “I would never say we can’t – I don’t believe that. But it’s about what we are capable of doing as a group.

“The run of form we had last season gives us a lot of confidence, but we know there is a whole new step to make. We are pushing to do that. It’s exciting. We have the potential to achieve things and we will definitely give it everything we can. We have to believe we are a good team and can do good things.”

United are hopeful of signing the midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton for less than £75m and remain in the market for a left-back. “We are looking to strengthen the squad, working towards that,” Carrick said. “We are trying to make the most of the opportunities to finish the window stronger than we went into it and are in a good way to doing that so far.”

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for as the new season kicks off
Sports.content:
1 Nwaneri out of Arsenal picture

While Myles Lewis-Skelly looks likely to remain at the Emirates, the same can’t be said for Ethan Nwaneri. The 19-year-old was outstanding in his breakthrough season for Arsenal in 2024-25 but barely featured last season and was sent on loan to Marseille. That didn’t really work out and Arsenal are now exploring another temporary move to ensure Nwaneri gets regular football this season. Milan, RB Leipzig, Dortmund and Fulham are all thought to be interested, with Nwaneri unlikely to feature on the bench for Friday’s opener against Coventry as a result. Whether Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus are available remains to be seen as Arsenal attempt to find suitors for the Brazil duo. Ed Aarons

Arsenal v Coventry City, Friday 8pm (all times BST)

2 New United pair down for Tigers test

Manchester United’s summer transfer business has focused on recruiting in central midfield. It will be interesting to see who Michael Carrick selects in two key roles for the first game of the season. Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have been present for more of pre-season than Kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute for England at the World Cup and was a late returner to Carrington after a holiday. Carlos Baleba surely will not have arrived in time to start at Hull. Mainoo is in the best position in the long term but if Carrick decides to ease him into the season, it would be intriguing to see how Santos and Tielemans team up, the stress test for a new partnership that could provide the perfect balance of defensive awareness and ability to move the team up the pitch. Will Unwin

Hull City v Manchester United, Saturday 12.30pm

3 Can Ipswich copy Black Cats’ success?

Ipswich clearly learned a lot from what Sunderland did a year ago, as they went out and bought a lot of players. The Black Cats quickly moulded their 19 acquisitions into a successful unit but at least they had the positive of a head coach in Régis Le Bris who had his feet under the table. Gary O’Neil is the new man at Portman Road and he has 12 signings – at time of writing – to potentially use for the opener. The record arrival, Emersonn, who has moved to Portman Road from Toulouse, is the most eye-catching of those who have been acquired. The Brazilian has an underwhelming career goalscoring record and a few question marks hanging over his head. Even though it is their first game, Ipswich need to pick up points at home, and to do so require a striker who can cause problems for defenders. How quickly Emersonn adapts will be critical for the Tractor Boys’ success this year. WU

Ipswich Town v Sunderland, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen Emersonn is one of a number of big-money signings made by promoted Ipswich this summer. Photograph: Keeran Marquis/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

4 Glasner’s tough Diomande ready for debut

August is the season for debuts and no one will be more satisfied than Oliver Glasner when Ousmane Diomande steps over the white line at the City Ground. Glasner wanted the Ivorian centre-back to replace Marc Guéhi at Crystal Palace, six months before the England defender departed for Manchester City. Diomande, a £34m buy from Sporting, is expected to line up in a back three for Nottingham Forest against Leeds, when the Austria midfielder Xaver Schlager, who played for Glasner at Wolfsburg, could also make his Forest bow. Diomande is a quick and physical defender but another aspect of his appeal is his aerial power at set pieces. “They’ve both played Champions League football and they are used to competing for titles,” said Glasner. “They can add this winning mentality.” Ben Fisher

Nottingham Forest v Leeds, Saturday 3pm

5 Serene Senesi can bring calm to Spurs

Cristian Romero has taken his maverick brand of defending to Atlético Madrid, upsetting neutral Premier League watchers. His compatriot Marcos Senesi has arrived to shore up things at the back as Roberto De Zerbi desperately tries to steer Spurs away from a third straight season of battling relegation. The all-action Romero had his qualities as a leader and defender but never felt dependable, which is what most want from a centre-back and captain. Senesi impressed during his time at Bournemouth, rarely making headlines but proving himself a calm presence at the back. The Argentinian is good on the ball and will be more adventurous in possession than his countryman. He is yet to be sent off in three seasons as a Premier League player – Romero was dismissed twice in 2025-26 alone, not to mention a one-match ban and a fine for his behaviour towards a referee. His calmness will improve Spurs. WU

Brentford v Tottenham, Saturday 5.30pm

6 Villa head south besieged by problems

It is surely not how Unai Emery envisaged the countdown to Aston Villa’s season-opener at Brighton on Sunday – and certainly not as he enjoyed the afterglow from the club’s Europa League triumph over Freiburg in May. The manager has an extraordinary number of problems. Take the midfield where the new signings João Gomes and Johan Manzambi are injury doubts. Note: Amadou Onana is a long-term casualty while Youri Tielemans has been sold. It goes on. Emery is about to lose Ezri Konsa to Arsenal – in a summer where Villa have also sold Morgan Rogers and Lucas Digne. They are trying to move on Emi Martínez, while the future of Ollie Watkins is uncertain, with Al-Hilal circling. For the cherry on top, the rampaging 17-year-old striker Brian Madjo is a fitness concern. Emery’s teamsheet will be very interesting. Will he pitch the new goalkeeper, Zion Suzuki, who only signed on Wednesday, straight in? David Hytner

Brighton v Aston Villa, Sunday 2pm

7 Maresca must win to silence City noise

Is Enzo Maresca already under pressure after Manchester City’s 3-0 schooling by Arsenal in the Community Shield? Maybe not, but if the Italian’s new team go down at home to Bournemouth on Sunday, you do not have to be a soothsayer to picture the scrutiny that will follow. Maresca and City are enduring a difficult transfer window, with Rodri’s departure to Barcelona the headline, a dizzying blow that has to be shaken off. The new Bournemouth coach, Marco Rose, has faced City six times in the Champions League with Leipzig and Mönchengladbach, and is sure to order his visitors to go for the jugular at the Etihad. City are vulnerable but Maresca can remedy this with a win of any sort. This, after all, is the job many felt he was the obvious choice for. Jamie Jackson

Manchester City v Bournemouth, Sunday 2pm

View image in fullscreen Anything but a win for Manchester City at home to Bournemouth will increase scrutiny on Enzo Maresca. Photograph: Dimitris Legakis/EPA

8 King Kev remembered at Newcastle

Kevin Keegan was supposed to have been the guest of honour at St James’ Park on Sunday, but his death from cancer in July means this meeting of two of his old clubs will turn into a tribute to one of English football’s enduring heroes. Keegan’s family will be present to witness an outpouring of love for the former Liverpool and Newcastle forward and (twice) Magpies manager. Once the game kicks off, all eyes will be on Alexander Isak, a St James’ Park old boy whose decision to force a £125m move to Anfield last summer did not go down well on Tyneside. The Sweden striker, making his first return to Newcastle, has much to prove at Liverpool, and now has a new head coach to impress in Andoni Iraola. Newcastle too have a new face in the home dugout, where Matthias Jaissle will occupy the technical area for so long inhabited by Eddie Howe. Louise Taylor

Newcastle v Liverpool, Sunday 4.30pm

9 Former Madrid managers meet in capital

Real Madrid’s two head coaches from last season meet at Craven Cottage, with the focus on Xabi Alonso, rather than Álvaro Arbeloa. The Fulham man, however, may have more to prove in the Premier League. His managerial career has been less prominent than that of his Basque rival – and he has clearly insisted on snapping up talent from the Bernabéu. Gonzalo García and César Palacios have made the trip over from the Spanish capital with Arbeloa. It shows great faith from the former Liverpool defender but it does put extra pressure on the trio, their fates now permanently intertwined. All three need a positive start to show they merit being in the Premier League. Otherwise, it would be very easily to criticise them individually and collectively. WU

Sports.title: Ronaldinho, 46, on mission of love and happiness – and maybe goals – at Serie C’s Ravenna
Sports.content:
It seemed like a joke, a hoax, when at 10pm on 19 June, Ravenna broke the news of Ronaldinho’s signing. The Brazilian, a former Ballon d’Or winner and one of the most recognisable figures in world football, had played his last official match in 2015 for Fluminense; a professional signing in Serie C at 46 years of age seemed unrealistic, to say the least. With football’s attention taken by the World Cup, the game was shocked by this bolt from the blue. For the most part, it remained in disbelief.

There was much discussion, in the city and around the world, about the real value of this operation, and we talked about it too, speaking with the mayor, the fans, and the president of Ravenna, Ignazio Cipriani, scion of the family known globally for Harry’s Bar, who is giving his city much more than a dream.

A dream that materialised, dispelling any doubts, at 11.50am on Thursday, when Ronaldinho, in a floral shirt and Bermuda shorts, with his now-familiar flat cap on his head, walked down the steps of the private jet that brought him from Milan Linate to the runway of Forlì airport. It is all true, all real. From there, he went on to the customary medical, like a true footballer. Ronaldinho is becoming a partner in the Ravenna club, as explained by the president, but he will also do his part on the pitch, with the dream of scoring the final goal of his career in the yellow-and-red jersey.

Then came the quick press conference, organised by the ownership at the Monaldina, the historic residence of the Gardini-Ferruzzi entrepreneurial family, the maternal dynasty from which Cipriani descends. There were few questions and hushed answers, very few words carefully chosen by Ronaldinho, who with his customary smile and gentle manners truly seems to have stepped back in time.

“The Milan derby is the most beautiful memory of my previous Italian experience,” began the former Barcelona and Milan No 10, before clarifying what drove him to Romagna: “Friendship and passion are the keys that brought me back here.”

He then clarified his goals in Ravenna: “To help, to excite the other players, and to have a spectacular season. To win, if possible.” Regarding his possible presence on the pitch, he explained: “If a goal comes, my experience in Ravenna will become even more beautiful, but whether I will actually play will be decided by the president and the coach.”

What does he think of the enthusiasm of Ravenna, a city that has literally gone crazy for him? Ronaldinho smiled and replied: “I just arrived, but I have a great desire to live this experience with the whole city.” His mission, he had already declared, is to bring happiness and love.

Echoing his words and capturing the essence of the city’s excitement was Ariedo Braida. Almost enunciating every word, the veteran executive summarised the operation with a striking remark: “We have the magic of football in Ravenna, what more could we ask for?”

View image in fullscreen Ronaldinho salutes onlookers but he will not participate in Ravenna’s opening Serie C game on Monday. Photograph: Massimo Paolone/LaPresse/Shutterstock

The former Milan and Barcelona director also recalled the opinion expressed by Kevin-Prince Boateng in 2016, according to which Ronaldinho holds the top spot in a ranking that also includes Pelé, Maradona, Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo.

Closing the circle was Cipriani himself, who revealed the behind-the-scenes of the miracle, after clarifying: “Ronaldinho is in shape.” When asked how he convinced the Brazilian champion, the answer was identical to that of the player: “Friendship and passion.” Cipriani then confirmed Ronaldinho’s entry as a shareholder in Ravenna FC, insisting on the profound meaning of the corporate move: “It’s not just about marketing, it’s not just international visibility. It is the chance to create a new enthusiasm around the club and the yellow-and-red jersey.”

Then the party began, organised in grand style on a stage set up on the beach at Marina di Ravenna, featuring the presentation of the entire Ravenna squad. The club’s president does not hide the ambition of a rapid climb to Serie B, with his sights set on the top flight. The star of the event, needless to say, was the Brazilian star, who for the first time presented himself before his new people, those Ravenna fans who back in June were curious, sceptical, or in disbelief.

Every doubt was dispelled on the beach of the ancient Byzantine capital, which today, with the arrival of the former Ballon d’Or winner, can truly dream big.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In living memory, the Romagnol city has never been talked about so much all over the world.

View image in fullscreen Ronaldinho’s unexpected comeback has captured fans’ imaginations, with 2,700 season tickets sold. Photograph: Stefano Rellandini/AFP/Getty Images

The fans didn’t just show up on the beach to celebrate their new idol, they also did so at the box office: the “Ronaldinho effect” has led to over 2,700 season tickets sold for Ravenna’s Serie C campaign, which kicks off on Monday in Reggio Emilia.

Ronaldinho, as confirmed by Cipriani, will not take part in the away match, but the fans hope to soon see him wearing the No 10 jersey, which was handed to him upon his arrival in Ravenna by the head coach, Andrea Mandorlini.

“Thank you very much,” are the words Ronaldinho dedicated to his celebrating people, while a child climbing the scaffolding of the giant screen shouted: “I saw him!”

He saw him at 46 years old, they had told him stories about him. Perhaps he will see him play again. This is the magic of football.

Sports.title: Man United boss Michael Carrick says it is 'ridiculous' to suggest they have an easy start against Hull and Ipswich - and plays down talk of a Premier League title challenge
Sports.content:
Man United boss Michael Carrick says it is 'ridiculous' to suggest they have an easy start against Hull and Ipswich - and plays down talk of a Premier League title challenge

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Michael Carrick says it’s ‘ridiculous’ to suggest Manchester United have been handed an easy start to the season – and admits it’s asking a lot for his team to be considered title challengers.

United kick off the campaign at Hull City on Saturday lunchtime followed by a first home game against another of the newly-promoted teams, Ipswich Town, at Old Trafford the following week.

But Carrick has rejected claims that United have been given an easy ride, saying: ‘There are no favourable starts. It’s an easy thing to throw out there but pretty ridiculous.

‘It’s a tough start against both teams, but we’re not getting past Saturday. A newly-promoted team away from home will be a tough game.

‘That is the beauty of the new season. For teams coming up into the league, there tend to be quite a few changes. That is the challenge playing against them, we are fully aware of that. Mentally and physically we have done a lot of work. We are fully aware of what’s at stake and what’s coming at us.’

On United’s chances of delivering a first Premier League title since 2013 while coping with the demands of a Champions League return, Carrick added: ‘It’s going to be a jump. It doesn’t matter whether I say whether we can or can’t – and I would never say we can’t – it’s about what we can do, and what we are capable of doing as a group.

Carrick has rejected claims that United have been handed an easy start to the season, saying: ‘There are no favourable starts. It’s an easy thing to throw out there but pretty ridiculous'

United hope to add a third midfield signing of the summer after tabling a £65million offer for Brighton’s Carlos Baleba (right)

‘The run of form we had last season gives us confidence, but we know there is a whole new step to make as a group. We have the potential to achieve things and we have to believe we can do good things.’

United hope to add a third midfield signing of the summer after tabling a £65million offer for Brighton’s Carlos Baleba, having already spent £85m on Andrey Santos, of Chelsea, and Aston Villa’s Youri Tielemans. The club are also keen to strengthen at left-back.

Carrick was reluctant to say too much with another 11 days to go until the transfer window closes. ‘I just think we are looking to strengthen the squad, and we are working towards that,’ he said. ‘We’re certainly trying to make the most of the opportunities to finish the window stronger than we went into it, and I think we are in a good way to doing that so far.’

Marcus Rashford’s return from a loan spell at Barcelona has given United another option, and Carrick has been delighted with the England international’s attitude so far.

‘It has been pretty obvious that Marcus came back training with Kobbie (Mainoo) and Licha (Martinez) that he has come back fantastically well,’ added the United boss. ‘He looks strong, sharp and ready to play football. He can play through the middle, even though it’s not his No 1 position. We have forwards that give us that flexibility.’

Carrick had some positive injury news with Mason Mount close to fitness after missing the final two friendlies against Leeds and AC Milan with a foot injury. Benjamin Sesko, Matthijs De Ligt and new No 2 goalkeeper Karl Darlow, none of whom featured in pre-season, are also back in training.

‘Karl has trained this week, he is in good shape,’ said Carrick. ‘Mattha has been out for a long period of time, but he is training, and it’s great to have him back. He won’t be involved but he is in good shape and moving in a good direction, so that is a bonus for us. Ben is back training so that is another positive and we’re looking forward to having him back around the group and getting him some minutes.

‘We’re managing Mason a little bit, but he is very close. He’s touch and go for the weekend really and going into next week. Mason will be back very, very soon, if not immediately, so it's all good.’

Sports.title: Liverpool expected to make improved offer for Brighton for winger Yankuba Minteh after £50m bid was rejected - with club still locked in talks with PSG in deal for Bradley Barcola
Sports.content:
Liverpool expected to make improved offer for Brighton for winger Yankuba Minteh after £50m bid was rejected - with club still locked in talks with PSG in deal for Bradley Barcola

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liverpool are expected to make an improved offer for Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh after having a £50m bid rejected.

The Gambian is out until October after undergoing surgery on his right leg.

Liverpool reverted to the 22-year-old after considering Ibrahim Mbaye of Paris St Germain too expensive. They are continuing discussions for Bradley Barcola.

Daily Mail Sport reported upon Mohamed Salah’s departure that the Gambia international would feature on a list to bolster the wide forward position this summer.

While talks for Barcola are ongoing, they would preferably like two forwards with Ibrahim Mbaye, also of PSG, one sounded out last week.

Minteh is currently on the sidelines after suffering an injury in Brighton's pre-season win over Roma earlier this month.

Liverpool have approached Brighton over signing winger Yankuba Minteh this summer

Andoni Iraola's side are in the market to sign two forwards, with the club locked in talks over PSG's Bradley Barcola

Minteh has made 73 appearances for Brighton to date since joining from Newcastle in a £30m move in the summer of 2024. He has scored 10 goals and provided nine assists for the Seagulls.

Minteh predominantly plays on the right wing, but has also been used on the left by Fabian Hurzeler.

Meanwhile, Curtis Jones will have a medical at noon on Friday after Liverpool agreed to sell him to Inter Milan for £26.7m plus £4m in bonuses and a 10 percent sell-on.

The six-time England international, who joined Liverpool aged nine, has had his heart set on a move to Serie A for some time after failing to regularly establish himself as a starter at Anfield.

Liverpool are preparing for their first season under new manager Andoni Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot following the Dutchman's dismissal at the end of last season.

After spending over £450million on new signings including Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer, the 2024-25 Premier League champions struggled to reach the same heights again under the Dutchman and only narrowly managed to qualify for the Champions League with a fifth-place finish last term.

Liverpool, who waved farewell to Mohamed Salah, Andrew Robertson and Ibrahima Konate at the start of the summer, have so far recruited centre-half Jeremy Jacquet from Stade Rennais and left winger Victor Munoz from Osasuna ahead of the new campaign.

Sports.title: RANGERS 1 JABLONEC 0: Ryan Naderi nets to nick a narrow lead but Ibrox men remain so unconvincing
Sports.content:
RANGERS 1 JABLONEC 0: Ryan Naderi nets to nick a narrow lead but Ibrox men remain so unconvincing

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

After taking a step forward with an emphatic victory over St Mirren in the Premier Sports Cup last weekend, this was a night when Rangers flirted with the idea of immediately taking two in the opposite direction.

In a UEFA Conference League play-off tie against Jablonec, Rangers made heavy weather of it - and then some.

A solitary goal from Ryan Naderi five minutes into the second half was enough to secure a one-goal lead as they head to the Czech Republic for next week's second leg.

But this is far from a done deal. Rangers remain far from convincing and no one can be sure that they will have group-stage football in Europe to look forward to for the season ahead.

The last time Rangers did not play in the group stage of a European competition was back in 2017 when they lost to Progres Niederkorn.

Derek McInnes and his players still have it all to do. Even against such limited opposition, Rangers were not impressive for the most part.

Ryan Naderi sees his effort hit the roof of the net to ensure Rangers take a first-leg lead

Rangers are denied as Jablonec defended stoutly at Ibrox

They were laborious in possession and largely devoid of creativity. They are still in the market for two new wingers and a new striker is possible.

It's not difficult to see why. The problem for McInnes is that he has already signed 11 new players. This is now very much his team and there looks to be precious little cohesion or attacking threat.

Rangers were clinging on towards the end after Cammy Devlin was shown a straight red card barely two minutes after coming off the bench.

It was a decision with which he could have no complaints, given it was high and it endangered his opponent.

If McInnes is to make a success of this job, it's difficult to overstate how important next week's return leg will be.

By hook or by crook, he and his players must come through it. If they were to be dumped out of Europe in two separate competitions by Jagiellonia Bialystok and Jablonec, it would be a major blot on his copybook.

Even this early in his tenure, he is fighting to convince some supporters he is the right man for the job. There is absolutely no style or identity to this team whatsoever.

Rangers were marginally improved in the second half but the overall paucity of the performance left the Ibrox crowd flat and underwhelmed, despite the slender victory.

When the Rangers team-sheet dropped prior to kick-off, more than a few eyebrows would have been raised at the fact Lawrence Shankland was once again on the bench.

McInnes had spoken pre-match about Shankland and insisted that he retained full confidence in the striker's ability to make a success of himself at Ibrox.

Yet, in a game of this magnitude, with European group-stage football on the line, there was something odd about the newly-appointed club captain not being in the starting XI.

Having deployed the team in a 4-3-3 shape in the 5-1 thrashing of St Mirren last weekend, McInnes clearly liked what he saw and stuck with it.

Naderi celebrates his goal, which could prove to be invaluable next week

Perhaps that's what went against Shankland, whose lack of mobility and ability to press makes him ill-suited to play the lone striker role in this system.

It was Ryan Naderi who got the nod up front, with the only change seeing Dan Neil coming in as captain to replace Nico Raskin in midfield.

For all they may not be the most glamorous of names to have graced Ibrox over the years, Jablonec arrived in confident mood on the back of six straight wins in all competitions.

The Czechs were quite content to sit in and frustrate Rangers in the early stages. In fairness, given the lack of creativity in the home side, it probably wasn't the most difficult of tasks.

Rangers lacked any guile or tempo in possession. Everything they did was one-paced and predictable, moving the ball from side to side, without any hint of penetration.

Manny Fernandez has been in poor form so far this season and it was notable just how nervous the crowd became when he was on the ball.

There looks to be a mistake in him at any moment. He picked up a booking after only 10 minutes and had to walk a tightrope for the remainder of the match.

As soon as Ben Godfrey is fit again, it is surely inevitable that he will come back into the team to partner Olwethu Makhanya and Fernandez will be dropped.

Rangers finally mustered a sight of goal on 25 minutes when some neat play in the penalty box saw Naderi lay the ball off to Vanja Dragojevic.

The Serbian midfielder had scored a screamer against St Mirren last weekend, but, on this occasion, his shot came back off the post and trickled along the goalline before the visitors were able to clear their lines.

Fernandez continued to be a bag of nerves. His body language was dreadful at times, moaning at others around him even though it was he who had made the mistake.

If there was a sense that the emphatic victory over St Mirren last weekend might imbue Rangers with a renewed sense of confidence, it simply did not materialise.

There were booed off at half-time. What made the performance so unimpressive was the fact that Jablonec were there for the taking.

Cammy Devlin saw red moments after coming on for Rangers as a second-half substitute

The Czechs could kindly be described as limited opposition. Even a semi-competent Rangers team would have been able to brush them aside with ease.

But this was another slog. The onus was on McInnes as manager to impart some kind of meaningful change heading into the second half.

With the crowd growing ever more restless, the breakthrough duly arrived within five minutes of the restart to ease the tension.

With what felt like his first forward pass all night, Neil clipped a ball to the back post, where Daisuke Yokota cushioned a header back across the face of goal.

With the goalkeeper out of position, Naderi, who had been largely anonymous, had the simple task of tapping home into the empty net.

The goal breathed new life into Rangers and it really ought to have been 2-0 just five minutes later when they cut the Czechs open down the right.

It was Naderi who whipped in a good cross to the far post for Djeidi Gassama. He met the ball first time on the volley and blazed it over when heading it may have been the better option.

Knowing that a one-goal lead would make for a nervy affair next week in the Czech Republic, Rangers were desperate to try and build on it if possible.

McInnes made a double change on 69 minutes, bringing on Devlin and Findlay Curtis as he tried to inject some fresh legs.

But it proved to be a disastrous cameo from Devlin, who, having only been on the pitch for a couple of minutes, went in late and high on Jablonec left-back Jiri Slama.

Romanian referee Marian Barbu appeared to miss the incident initially, but, after being referred to the monitor by the VAR, he showed Devlin a straight red card.

This was desperate for Rangers. It was now a case of backs to the wall and trying to cling on against a team who would be no more than mid-table in the Scottish Premiership.

They got the job done in the end, but it was a tough watch. Truth be told, they will settle for more of the same next week if the end result is a place in the group stage.

Sports.title: Man United progressing in Carlos Baleba talks with Brighton, Aston Villa table Ollie Watkins contract offer amid Saudi interest, and Man City see Adam Wharton enquiry rebuffed: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season. Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team... Man United progressing in Baleba talks Manchester United are continuing discussions over a fee with Brighton for Carlos Baleba. Brighton have rejected United’s £60million plus £5m for the midfielder but talks have been progressing to a compromise. The 22-year-old Cameroon international is hoping the deal can be wrapped up over the weekend. Meanwhile, United right-back Habeeb Ogunneye is scheduled to undergo a medical with Arsenal ahead of his move there. The deal is understood to be a free transfer with 40percent sell-on clause. The 20-year-old is being signed to boost numbers with Arsenal’s U21s but also train with the first team. Man United have had a £65m offer for Carlos Baleba rejected but talks are progressing with Brighton Clubs circle for Jackson Atletico Madrid have enquired about a loan deal for Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson. Atletico director Mateu Alemany was understood to have travelled to London on Thursday for talks. Jackson also has interest from Aston Villa, Napoli and Saudi Arabia. Meanwhile Chelsea forward Deivid Washington is a target for Marseilla, Strasbourg and Sevilla. Blues defender Axel Disasi is continuing to discuss a loan move to Crystal Palace while Benoit Badiashile is joining Napoli. Leeds United are interested in striker Liam Delap as are Everton. Spurs talk numbers Tottenham are working on figures with City for Savinho and forward Omar Marmoush. The deal for Savinho could be worth up to £84m. City have also asked about Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton as they work through a list of targets. Leeds swoop for goalkeeper Zetterer Leeds United are closing on a deal for Eintracht Frankfurt goalkeeper Michael Zetterer to come in as James Trafford's deputy. The clubs are finalising agreement for the 31-year-old, but Frankfurt need to find a new goalkeeper to replace Zetterer first. Leeds are waiting for Lucas Perri to fully recover from a minor injury before he completes his delayed loan move to Torino. Zetterer, 31, is a former Germany U21 international. Southampton reject Villa approach for Harwood-Bellis Aston Villa have been rebuffed in an enquiry for Southampton defender Taylor Harwood-Bellis. Villa are willing to offer around £17.5m for the 24-year-old but Saints had already rejected a similar offer from Benfica. Talks are ongoing as Villa assess options such as Tosin Adarabioyo at Chelsea and Fikayo Tomori of AC Milan to fill the void left by Ezri Konsa's move to Arsenal. Villa have been rebuffed in an enquiry for Southampton defender Taylor Harwood-Bellis City keep watching brief on Wharton Manchester City maintain an interest in Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton. The Selhurst Park club are reluctant to lose the 22-year-old this summer but have been making significant enquiries for midfielders in recent weeks. City are exploring several options including Manu Kone at Roma while they are advancing in talks to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille and are assessing the cost of a bid for Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez. 'We did it [sold big players in the past], and now is not the moment to do that,' said Palace boss Pierre Sage on Thursday. 'He is able to play in another club, a big club. Here, or anywhere in Europe, but one year with us, in a new dynamic, will be good for him. And we need him - that is why I think he will stay with us.' Wharton has been a significant Premier League performer in recent seasons and excelled in the Europa League Conference final but analysts at some top level would-be suitors have indicated his running statistics do not reflect someone who can fit into a high-pressing style. He continues to show on the pitch, however, an ability to find the right pass and shield his defence. City have also made contact with Palmeiras for winger Allan Elias as they seek a replacement for Savinho. Allan, 22, wants to join City but his club are reluctant to sell now with their season running to December. Talks are ongoing over a £35million fee. SIMON JONES AND BOBBY MANZI Manchester City have seen an enquiry for Adam Wharton rebuffed by Crystal Palace Jones set for Inter medical Inter Milan expect Curtis Jones to arrive later today ahead of a £30.7million move from Liverpool. The Italian side have scheduled Jones' medical for midday on Friday. Inter bid £26.7m plus £4m in add-ons with a 10 per cent sell-on clause, offering a similar structure to the deal used to sign Djed Spence from Tottenham. Curtis Jones is set to sign a five-year deal with Inter Jones, 25, will sign a five-year deal with the Serie A champions. Meanwhile, Liverpool centre back Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, is in talks to join Levante on loan. Ndukwe does not qualify for a work permit in England so must be loaned out. Liverpool remain in talks over PSG winger Bradley Barcola. Sheffield Wednesday are to confirm the signing of Liverpool's Northern Ireland international winger Kieran Morrison on a season-long loan. Hammers close on Mukasa West Ham are close to an agreement to sign highly-rated Manchester City forward Divine Mukasa on loan for the season. There is no buy option for the 18-year-old who spent the second half of last season on loan at Leicester City City step up hunt for Savinho replacement Manchester City have asked about Palmeiras winger Allan Elias as they consider replacements for Savinho. Allan is 22 but has not been capped by Brazil. Quick and skilful, he is not a goalscorer but has earned a reputation as a worker, willing to press. Newcastle United and Aston Villa have also scouted him in recent months. City are evaluating several options with Tottenham working on the deal to sign Savinho and forward Omar Marmoush. Bayern reach Palhinha agreement Bayern Munich have reached a full agreement with Benfica over the £17million sale of Joao Palhinha. The 31-year-old midfielder had been a target for Aston Villa and Newcastle United but will now reunite with his former Fulham boss Marco Silva at Benfica. Villa were only willing to take him on an initial loan which Bayern refused. Villa table new contract offer to Watkins Aston Villa have made a new contract offer to striker Ollie Watkins. The 30-year-old is open to a move to Al Hilal who had a £38.5m offer rejected on Tuesday but are preparing a fourth offer for the England international. Watkins has scored consistently throughout his Villa career and his goals would be difficult to replace. Villa have maintained contacts over Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson who also has interest from Napoli but he is valued around £65m. Aston Villa have put forward a new contract offer to striker Ollie Watkins Wrexham make move for ex-United star Wrexham are continuing discussions with free agent Axel Tuanzebe. The 28-year-old Congo international left Burnley at the end of last season and has had interest from clubs but is interested in Wrexham's ambitious project. Wrexham are in talks to sign former Manchester United defender Axel Tuanzebe Palace return for Auxerre target Crystal Palace have rekindled interest in Auxerre midfielder Kevin Danois. The 22-year-old was discussed as an option in January and Palace have made further enquiries. The France U21 international is an attacking player who can also play out wide and was on Newcastle United's list earlier in the year. Hull advance in talks for Betis star Garcia Hull City owner Acun Ilicali has confirmed they are making progress on their bid to sign Real Betis winger Pablo Garcia and remain in talks for Deportivo La Coruna winger Yeremay Hernandez. 'I think probably, if nothing unknown happens, we will see him in a black and gold shirt. It has to be finalised, but I would say 90 percent of this deal is done. We are talking about the last details,' said Ilicali. Pictures of Hernandez in Hull have been posted on social media, and Ilicali told BBC Humberside: 'We have to get the club side done and Yeremay also wants to come but it is a very vital, critical decision for himself. This deal is a very hard deal but we are somewhere where it looks positive. 'He is a young boy and it would change his life completely so he wanted to see where he would come. We will see in three, four days if this deal will be done or not. If it happens it will be a record for sure.' Race on for Black Cats Ta Bi West Ham and Burnley have expressed interest in Sunderland winger Jocelin Ta Bi. The 21-year-old only joined Sunderland from Maccabi Netanya in January and signed a four and a half year contract. He made one appearance in the FA Cup against Oxford United and then started against Fulham in the Premier League. As it stands, the Championship clubs have expressed interest but talks have not gone further. Wolves 'keeper Dan Bentley has joined Coventry City on a free as back up to Carl Rushworth. Charlton are signing Wrexham goalkeeper Arthur Okonkwo on a season loan. Stoke are keen on Manu Duah from San Diego.
